tagline: Accelerating the energy transition across Europe and North America through renewable capacity expansion and grid modernization.
hero_kpi_rationale: EDP is a pure-play renewable energy player in Europe and North America, with a clear growth trajectory in solar and wind. This KPI captures the core of its growth and decarbonization strategy.

kpis.name: Installed Renewable Capacity
kpis.explanation: Total power output from operational wind and solar farms.
kpis.description: Installed capacity in renewable energy (wind + solar) as of end-2025. EDP is focusing on rapid expansion in the United States and Brazil.
kpis.signal: Strong growth driven by solar in the U.S. and Iberia.

kpis.name: EBITDA
kpis.description: Consolidated EBITDA in 2025, driven by grid operations and renewables.
kpis.signal: Sustained growth supported by electricity demand and grid infrastructure.

kpis.name: Investments (Capex)
kpis.explanation: Annual capital expenditures for new infrastructure.
kpis.description: Total capex in 2025, including a €3.0 billion investment plan announced for the Portuguese distribution grid (2026–2030).
kpis.signal: Marked acceleration in investments, particularly in Portugal.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.description: Consolidated gross margin, benefiting from the low cost variability of renewable assets.
kpis.signal: Improvement linked to the ramp-up of low-cost renewable assets.

kpis.name: Headcount (employees)
kpis.explanation: Total number of employees in the group.
kpis.description: Total headcount as of end-2025, reflecting disciplined human resource management.
kpis.signal: Stable workforce despite growth, indicating operational efficiency.

kpis.name: Renewables Investment Share
kpis.explanation: Proportion of total capex allocated to renewable energy.
kpis.description: In 2025, 60% of total capex was allocated to renewables, primarily in the U.S. and Iberia.
kpis.signal: Clear priority given to green growth.

kpis.name: Dividend per Share
kpis.description: Annual dividend per share paid, aggregated from yfinance.dividends over the last seven fiscal years reported by the company.
kpis.signal: Dividend per share of $2.405 in the latest year.

kpis.name: Capital Returned (dividends)
kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders via annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow over the last four fiscal years reported.
kpis.signal: Capital returned to shareholders via dividends of $0.827 billion in the latest year.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.description: Payout Ratio = Dividends Paid / Net Income, calculated over the last four fiscal years from yfinance.cashflow and yfinance.income_stmt.
kpis.signal: Share of net income distributed as dividends: 71.9% in the latest year.

kpis.name: North America EBITDA Share
kpis.explanation: Contribution of North American operations to operating profit.
kpis.description: In 2025, 60% of EBITDA came from North America. This share is expected to reach 68% by 2028.
kpis.signal: Geographic transformation of the group toward the U.S.

kpis.name: Network Investment Portugal
kpis.explanation: Planned investment amount in the Portuguese distribution grid.
kpis.description: EDP will invest €3.0 billion between 2026 and 2030 in the distribution grid, +70% versus the prior period.
kpis.signal: Major acceleration to strengthen resilience after storms.

kpis.name: Earnings per Share
kpis.explanation: Net income divided by the weighted average number of diluted shares outstanding during the fiscal year. Measures the company's ability to generate profit per share: basis for Payout Ratio calculation (DPS / EPS).
kpis.description: 5-year history (2021-2025). Source: yfinance income statement (Diluted EPS).

risks.title: Dependence on electricity grid regulation
risks.summary: EDP is highly dependent on regulatory approvals for its grid revenues. Regulatory frameworks in Portugal, Spain, and Brazil define return rates (6.58%-12%) and concession periods. Any adverse change in these parameters (RoRAB, concession duration, tariff model) would directly impact the profitability of distribution and transmission activities.
risks.score_rationale: Major risk for EDP: grids represent 31% of 2025 EBITDA and are fully dependent on regulatory frameworks (Portugal 2026-2029, Spain 2026-2031, Brazil until 2027-2030). Moderate language but central position in the 2026-28 strategy (€7Bn net investments). Stable trend with displayed regulatory visibility.

risks.title: Geopolitical risks affecting supply chains
risks.summary: Ongoing conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East are disrupting logistics chains and energy markets. EDP, with a global presence (Europe, North/South America, Asia-Pacific), is exposed to supply chain disruptions, commodity price volatility, and trade restrictions. The U.S. Equipment Sourcing Rule (minimum 40% non-FEOC sourcing) complicates equipment procurement for U.S. projects.
risks.score_rationale: Explicit language on Ukraine/Middle East conflicts, logistical disruptions, and energy volatility. Position at the beginning of the document (section 3.1.1) indicates strategic importance. EDP operates in Europe, North/South America, and Asia-Pacific, exposed to these risks. Trend increasing with mention of 'sustained geopolitical fragmentation'.

risks.title: U.S. federal regulatory uncertainty on renewable energy
risks.summary: The new U.S. administration has recalibrated federal priorities, creating regulatory uncertainty for renewable energy. While state-level initiatives and corporate commitments support investments, executive actions, departmental memos (Interior, Energy, Transportation), and revisions to tax credits (PTC, ITC) threaten the viability of U.S. projects. EDP plans 531 MW of additions in 2025 in North America.
risks.score_rationale: Explicit warning language: 'significant policy disruption in 2025' and 'regulatory uncertainty remains'. EDP Renewables represents 39% of 2025 EBITDA and 62% of 2025 gross investments (€3.9Bn). North America = 30% of installed capacity. Trend increasing with executive actions and federal policy revisions.

risks.title: Occupational health and safety in operations and subcontracting
risks.summary: EDP recorded 3 contractor fatalities in 2025 despite a 56% reduction in serious accidents. Management acknowledges the need to strengthen oversight of partners and subcontractors. Risks include litigation, regulatory fines, reputational damage, and operational disruptions. The 'Zero SIF' objective underscores the perceived severity of the risk.
risks.score_rationale: Strong language: 'not acceptable', 'Zero Serious Injuries and Fatalities' as an objective. Three contractor fatalities in 2025 despite 56% improvement in SIFs. Position at the beginning of the document (Management Statement) indicates strategic priority. High risk of reputational damage, litigation, and civil liability.

risks.title: Dependence on long-term contracts and capacity auctions
risks.summary: EDP relies heavily on long-term contracts and capacity auctions to secure revenues from renewable generation. In Brazil, regulation must address the impact of curtailment on renewables. In the U.S., auctions for long-term contracts (322 MW with Energa Obrót, 454 MW in California) are critical. Any reduction in demand or competitiveness in auctions would impact projected growth.
risks.score_rationale: EDP targets 80% of EBITDA in A-rated, regulated markets and long-term contracts (2028). Moderate but strategic language: 'distinctive and resilient portfolio'. Risk of concentration on existing contracts and dependence on future auctions (Brazil, U.S.). Stable trend with displayed visibility.

risks.title: Project permitting risks and commissioning delays
risks.summary: Federal permits for wind and solar projects in the U.S. face significant political disruptions in 2025. EDP has 322 MW under construction with commissioning expected between 2026 and 2029. Permitting delays (1-3 years) and executive actions can delay FID and COD, impacting investment timelines and expected returns.
risks.score_rationale: Explicit language on 'Federal permitting for wind and solar projects has faced significant policy disruption'. EDP plans 2.1 GW of additions in 2025 (100% renewables/BESS) with permitting delays of 1-3 years. Risk of delays on 322 MW under construction (2026-2029). Trend increasing with federal disruptions mentioned.

risks.title: Electricity and commodity price volatility
risks.summary: Geopolitical conflicts and logistical disruptions are causing volatility in electricity and commodity prices. EDP increased thermal generation by 149% in 2025 to meet demand for flexibility services in Iberia. This exposure to spot prices and fuel costs creates margin risk on unhedged or short-term contracts.
risks.score_rationale: Moderate language but explicit context: 'volatility in energy and commodity markets' due to geopolitical conflicts. EDP generated 64.2 TWh in 2025 with 10% thermal (CCGT) for flexibility services. Stable trend but sensitivity to external shocks. Margin risk on unhedged contracts.

risks.title: Curtailment and grid integration risks in Latin America
risks.summary: In Brazil, renewable curtailment is an increasing risk due to regional imbalances between generation and urban demand. EDP operates EDP Espírito Santo (5 years, ~12% RoR) and EDP São Paulo (5 years, 11% RoR). Brazilian regulation must address this impact. Any delay or insufficient compensation would reduce revenues from Brazilian assets.
risks.score_rationale: Explicit language: 'regulation is expected to address curtailment impact on renewables' in Brazil. EDP Espírito Santo and EDP São Paulo represent 4% of installed capacity. Risk of revenue reduction if curtailment is not compensated. Stable trend with regulation in evolution.

ai_positioning.summary: EDP mentions the acceleration of electricity demand driven by AI (data centers), but does not position AI as a central technological lever for its operations or services.
evidence: Global electricity demand is accelerating driven by AI, industrial electrification, and electric mobility
rapid expansion of data centers across the U.S.
